key_insight: X-AgentRed finds harmful cross-service agent behaviors by building and evolving a tool-dependency graph instead of relying only on prompted attack generation.
engineering_relevance: For personal agents that act across multiple apps and services, this offers a practical way to stress-test tool chains and uncover risky compositional failures before deployment.
method: Analyze each tool’s effects, harms, and execution preconditions.
Build a directed graph where one tool’s effects can satisfy another tool’s requirements.
Sample graph recipes into realistic scenarios, then use execution feedback to diversify tool substitutions and refine blocked preconditions.
evidence_signal: Across four frontier agentic models, the method reached 1.77× the harmful path rate of STAC and 2.99× average tool coverage.
watch_item: Because it relies on modeled tool effects and preconditions, performance may depend on how accurately the ecosystem is described and may miss harms outside the constructed graph.
paper_title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
